chunks: From him, from Abu Hammam, from Al-Rida (peace be upon him)

key_terms.الرِّضَا: Al-Rida (peace be upon him), referring to Imam Ali al-Rida, the eighth Imam
key_terms.مِثْلَهُ: Like it / The same as it

ai.seo_question: What does the phrase 'mithlahu' mean in Shia hadith literature?
ai.summary: This concise narration from Imam al-Rida (AS) in *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* confirms the continuity of the ruling regarding the ambiguous will (*Al-Wasiyyah al-Mubhama*), where the specific beneficiary is not explicitly named. It highlights the scholarly tradition of using 'mithluha' (like it) to link rulings within the chapter, emphasizing the consistency of Imami jurisprudence on testamentary ambiguity as recorded by Shaykh al-Tusi.
